analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: the new changelog (changelog.d/nemotron-super-media-discovery.md), a paragraph in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md lines 13-18, and docs/architecture/inference.md. For inference.md only metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied, so its text is not verified. No Swift source was provided, so every claim about the Nemotron Super local owner, builder and HTTP hook is unverified. The changelog describes new, unregistered, opt-in surfaces:
- An HTTP text/image hook "using existing auth", disabled by default. It accepts consumer-provided inline PNG/JPEG decoded by a CPU decoder in the provider process. Relevant: TB-007, T-050 (media plaintext handling) and A-001. The decoder-bounds and allocation claims are untested here.
- Env-gated MTP speculation and concurrency up to 8.
- A resident recurrent checkpoint bank (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1), which conflicts with T-041's statement that production creates no RAM prefix tier (reported as a low finding).
The docs also say the builder requires a live pending LOAD lease and preserves the fixed-workspace concurrency floor (hardware-support.md 13-18), which is consistent with the memory-admission invariants. Next pass should check: the cache key and scope of the checkpoint bank, the auth on the hook, image decoder bounds, KV/activation reservation accounting, and whether the plaintext hook bypasses the coordinator's E2E/attestation path (TB-002, TB-011). No source files were available to confirm these.

findings.detail: The changelog adds `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, which opts the Nemotron Super owner into a resident recurrent checkpoint bank for exact text prefix reuse. The bank is sized from the KV grant and its budget is reserved from load until retirement. T-041 and its mitigations state that production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache, and that the only tier is the encrypted SSD tier with coordinator-authored account/model cacheSalt scoping. The changelog says client prompt-cache keys are rejected. It does not say whether the bank is keyed by the coordinator's authenticated cacheSalt, so cross-account reuse and TTFT timing leakage through this tier cannot be ruled out from the supplied text. The bank also has no stated TTL, KEK protection or purge: checkpoints are plaintext recurrent state in process RAM. This is the SEC-035 oracle class, and also affects T-028/T-011 residue in process memory. The path is opt-in and its builder is described as unregistered, so this is a threat-model gap rather than a confirmed regression. Fix: before the hook is registered, extend T-041 with this tier's scoping, lifetime, wipe-on-retirement and timing posture, and require the coordinator cacheSalt in the bank key.
findings.title: Opt-in resident-RAM prefix-cache bank contradicts T-041's "no production RAM tier" posture
